title: Blocks (Reactive/Mobile): own block definition (inputs, placeholders, events, triggers), block instances configured in a consumer, referenced block signatures (read-only)

capabilities.title: Own reusable block definition: parameters, placeholders, its own block-level triggers
capabilities.summary: `create IMobileBlock` in a UI flow with input parameters and local variables (logic elements), IPlaceholderWidget (the extension point each instance fills), IBlockEvent (IsMandatory, parameters) fired by an ITriggerNode in a block screen action (`set $trg Event $ev`). The definition is edited here; instances are configured in ui.block-instance.

route.operation: create IMobileBlock in IMobileFlow:<Flow>; create IPlaceholderWidget, IBlockEvent (+ input parameters), ITriggerNode in a block screen action; set Event/IsMandatory/Description/StyleSheet; usages before delete

capabilities.guidance: Placeholder content written inside the block is example content: the platform copies it into each instance's IPlaceholderContentWidget, where it belongs to the consumer. Changing an event contract (a new parameter, IsMandatory) breaks the trigger in the producer and leaves each consumer handler with an empty argument to fill; instances keep their handler key. Delete order: consumers first (instance handlers and instances in the screens, then the triggers), then the event or the block.

limits.text: Changing an event contract breaks the trigger (the producer's arguments mirror the event parameters), not the consumer handlers; the IEventHandler exists even without a handler and counts in usages.
`rename` of an IBlockEvent returns success but writes nothing on ODC in this build: rename its neighbours (trigger node, handler action) instead.
A mandatory event without handler is not refused by the kernel: Verify reports one EventHandlerRequiredAction error per instance.
Block events have the same behaviour on O11 and ODC (5 positive jobs and 1 negative on each lane); IsMandatory without handler is an error per instance.
Evolving a PUBLIC block is guarded: removing Public, removing or retyping an input, or adding a mandatory input without migrating consumers is refused by the screen contract.

recommends.when: the block screen action that holds the trigger node

capabilities.title: Instantiate an existing block (own or from a referenced library such as OutSystemsUI) and configure the instance: arguments, handlers, placeholder content
capabilities.summary: An instance (`IMobileBlockInstanceWidget`) points at a block with `source`/`SourceBlock` (own `IMobileBlock:<Name>` or a referenced block resolved through its signature). The consumer configures only the instance: input values (`set $inst/<Input> Value <expr>`), event handlers (`set $inst/<Event> Handler <screen action>` plus `set $inst/<Event>/<Param> Value`), and the content of each placeholder (widgets created under `$inst/<Placeholder>`, or `<slot name>` in html-visual). The visual `html` op writes the same thing from `<Block name :Input @Event><slot>`. The referenced block's inputs, events and placeholders are its signature: read them from the capture, never from curated text; the signature is edited only in its producer.

route.operation: create {parent, type: IMobileBlockInstanceWidget, name, source: 'IMobileBlock:<Block>', empty?}; set $inst/<Input> Value; set $inst/<Event> Handler; create widgets under $inst/<Placeholder>; or the fragment {"op":"html","parent":"<widget path>","html":"<Block name=\"B\" :Input=\"expr\" @Event=\"ScreenAction\"><slot name=\"Placeholder\">...</slot></Block>"}

capabilities.guidance: List what the module already references (--app: context.reads MobileBlockSignature) before choosing a block; a block from a library that the module does not reference yet needs the reference first (C: reference.*; not headless on ODC). A library block born with example content keeps it unless `empty: true`; a placeholder born with an Input is bound with `set .../#IInput Variable`, not emptied. A block instance has no Variable of its own: values reach the screen through the handler of an event. Components of third-party libraries are only known through the signature of the referenced revision; nothing here promises a catalog of every library component.

limits.text: Only the DatePicker OutSystemsUI block has an ODC job; the other patterns (Tabs, Accordion, Search, Pagination, DropdownSearch...) are not exercised on ODC. Placeholders born with an Input are bound with `set .../#IInput Variable`, not `empty`.
Adding a new library reference is not headless on the ODC kernel (reference-import-headless): instance only blocks the module already references.
A hidden (indirect) reference to a library block is unhidden by the verb when SourceBlock is bound; otherwise the automatic 3-way merge dropped the handlers and arguments.
The offline OutSystemsUI catalog (kernel/catalog/ui, 2.28.1) is not used by jobs nor by this answer: the contract of a library block is the signature in the module.

differences: library blocks are instanced in Reactive (MainContent) and Mobile (Content) modules alike

recommends.when: the screen action named as Handler of an instance event
